retro:
# PR #12834 retrospective

## Worked

Current author eligibility checked with shared gate. Read-only security triage preceded reviewer launches. Both technical reviewers had verified new native sessions at required models/efforts and equivalent neutral public-history scope. Peer reports stayed unread until both finals existed. Source-only Sol assessment and Opus source reasoning independently resolved the material questions. A short comparison table explains both fixes without filling a no-findings review with speculative advice.

## Deviations and retained history

Initial coordinator registry metadata output exceeded the aggregate output bound; initial 60-line workflow chunks did not reserve tool metadata overhead. Later reads use 50 content lines. No source execution relied on these administrative outputs. Both real dispatches repeated the first-call constraints.

Initial Opus start was rejected for multiline argument encoding. The unique failed receipt remains; second attempt flattened only whitespace and started one fresh session. Herdr documentation command returned its documented syntax status and compliance-shell agent query returned no agent; neither was a model failure. Unique lifecycle receipt paths preserve each attempt.

Opus's first isolated fixture failed on an incorrect expectation that migration stdout was empty. V2 corrected that expectation but audit found ungated mkdir/chmod/printf and helper producers, missing intermediate mkdir targets, TMPDIR containment rather than individual mktemp-file assertion, payload reading before child status gate, and unchecked find status. Preserve both sealed runs and full audit addendum. Broad totals and full-compliance claims are excluded. Some fetch decodes relied on a manually observed successful HTTP status instead of a scripted gate; raw transport and failure history remain preserved. Sol's wc attempt included directories and emitted directory errors; no claim depended on counts.

## Remediation and publishability

The reviewer received exact audit corrections after independent finals and saved an addendum without rewriting history. No more substitute fixtures were needed: current pinned source establishes every public claim. Public test scope does not claim execution success. Process remains explicitly noncompliant; technical source evidence and independence are sound within the stated limits. This process-only deviation does not require a posting hold once editorial/freshness checks pass.

For future assignments, use a literal per-callee final-target/status inventory including intermediate mkdir paths, redirects, stubs and interpreter/utility temps; implement gates rather than listing them. Evaluate expected child status before payload. Prefer source-only review when it already settles the material question. These rules are already in the current workflow and repeated in this assignment; the failure was implementation, not missing instructions.

## Resources

No desktop slots, browser or host services used. Runtime runs were private review.py namespaces and finished, with no background fixture children. Preserve all evidence and reviewer panes. No intentional native memory writes. No Omadev tool bug established.

The previously resolved generated-shortcut issue remains addressed: the old generated command is repaired, while fresh installations omit the flag. The distinct `--ignore-certificate-errors-spki-list` switch remains allowed, and unrelated arguments are forwarded in their original form. These are scoped source conclusions, not whole-PR approval.

---
